newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips lower, following bond market slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips lower, following bond market slide.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares slumped in afternoon trading on Wednesday, tracking the bond market lower and hit by a bout of profit-taking after a rally inspired by a Federal Reserve decision to let rates stand.

The Dow industrial average was trading off around 57 points at 7247 in heavy volume, well under its intraday high of 7353. The New York stock exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at around 1249 EDT/1649 GMT.
The inflation-wary long bond moved down 30/32 at a 6.98 percent yield, sinking after data which showed a sharp narrowing of the U.S. trade gap in March.
The U.S. trade deficit narrowed 19.3 percent in March to $8.51 billion compared with a forecast $10.3 billion gap.
"The stock market is following the bond market like a mirror image," Tom Carpenter, a managing director and chief economist at ASB Capital Management, said.
But he said the stock market was trading close to record highs, and some consolidation was normal.
Meanwhile, Nasdaq stayed steady for most of the day, boosted by strength in the technology sector and strong first quarter earnings from Dell Computer Corp.
